A '''testimator''' is an [[estimator]] whose value depends on the result of a test for [[statistical significance]]. In the simplest case the value of the final estimator is that of the basic [[estimator]] if the test result is significant, and otherwise the value is zero. However more general testimators are possible.<ref>Adke, S.R., Waikar, V.B. & Schurmann, F.J. (1987). "A two stage shrinkage testimator for the mean of an exponential distribution". [[Communications in Statistics#Communications in Statistics – Simulation and Computation|Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods]], 16 (6), 1821-1834. Retrieved April 16, 2009, from http://www.informaworld.com/10.1080/03610928708829474 (restricted access)</ref>

==History==
An early use of the term "testimator" way made by Brewster & Zidek (1974).<ref>Brewster, J.F., Zidek, J.V.(1974) "Improving on Equivariant Estimators". [[Annals of Statistics]], 2 (1), 21&ndash;38</ref>
